Morgana.wikitext:
{{ChaosPortal}}
'''Morgana''' was a [[Chaos]] witch, who seduced the [[Planetary Governor]] of the planet [[Vespa]] to Chaos worship.{{Fn|1}}

This soon caused the planet to fall to the [[Ruinous Powers]] and began the populations' rebellion against the [[Imperium]]{{Fn|1}}, but when word of their fall reached the  [[Blood Ravens]] [[Chapter]], they launched the [[Vespa Crusade]] to reclaim the planet{{Fn|2a}}. Soon war would engulf Vespa, as the Blood Ravens fought their way to Morgana's stronghold, the Black Abbey, to end the rebellion. Morgana would not go easily though and she slayed the Blood Ravens' expedition leader and most of his staff with her [[psychic]] powers; before finally being killed by the young initiate [[Davian Thule]]. After Morgana's death the Blood Ravens purged all life from Vespa, to ensure the taint of Chaos was completely destroyed.{{Fn|1}}

(Former) *[[Black Legion]] **[[Ezekarion]] |Notes = }} '''Moriana''' is the damned seer of [[Ezekyle Abaddon|Abaddon the Despoiler]]. ===History=== ====Origins==== Moriana's origins are shrouded in mystery. There are several individual mentions of her throughout various sources: *According to [[Iron Warriors]] [[Warsmith]] [[Honsou]], it was rumoured that she was once a handmaiden to the [[Emperor of Mankind]], before she fell from grace and was banished from the [[Imperium]]{{Fn|1}}. *[[Moriana Mouhausen]] was one of the [[Chosen of Malcador]] and was amongst those the [[Malcador the Sigillite|The Sigillite]] summoned before he took his place upon the [[Golden Throne]] during the final stages of the [[Siege of Terra]]. Like her colleague [[Zaranchek Xanthus]], Moriana sought to obtain the anti-[[Astartes]] weapon and its creator [[Basilio Fo]] from [[Custodes]] custody, feeling it belonged to the Sigillite's Chosen.{{Fn|5}} *The Blessed Lady of the [[Word Bearers]], powerful [[Psyker]], and artificial [[Perpetual]] [[Cyrene Valantion]]/[[Actae]] took on the name Moriana after the [[Siege of Terra]]. During the battle, her mind became melded with [[Katerina Moriana]], one of the [[Argonauts]].{{Fn|6}} ====Abaddon's Seer==== After the Heresy, it is said that Moriana was one of the few members of the [[Horusians]] within the nascent [[Inquisition]], a sect which believed that the dark power which had animated [[Horus Lupercal]] during the [[Horus Heresy]] could be harnessed to resurrect the fallen Emperor. The Horusians were regarded with fear and suspicion by the rest of the Inquisition and consequently trod carefully, while some, like Moriana, fell to [[Chaos]]{{Fn|2}}. [[Iskandar Khayon]] claims that he met her in the Tomb of Horus on [[Maeleum]], where she told him of the current state of the Imperium. Upon returning to the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]'' with her, she told Abaddon that the death of [[Thagus Daravek]] was a critical part of his destiny, because no future she saw had both of them alive.{{Fn|3}} Whatever the truth, she was an incredibly powerful [[psyker]] with a gift of clairvoyance that led to her being consulted frequently by [[Warmaster]] Abaddon. Honsou's lieutenant, [[Cadaras Grendel]], snorted that this was hardly a rousing endorsement, considering the failure of Abaddon's twelve (at that time) previous [[Black Crusades]]. But Honsou countered that it was largely thanks to Moriana's counsel that Abaddon was able to seize the coveted [[Blackstone Fortress]]es during the [[Gothic War]].{{Fn|1}} At some point in the 900's [[M41]], a [[Deathwatch]] kill-team led by [[Uriel Ventris]] tracked down Moriana's lair and attempted to kill her, but without success{{Fn|1}}. Honsou tracked down her lair on an unnamed planet, seeking advice on how to find and revive the [[Daemon Prince]] [[M'kar]], a vital ally for Honsou's planned [[invasion of Ultramar]]. Moriana agreed to help him, asking only for his blood oath that he would prosecute his campaign to the bitter end, no matter what. It seemed that Moriana was largely indifferent to the designs of Chaos, and gave deference to no one, including Abaddon, but was still moved by hatred of the Imperium.{{Fn|1}} She also helped the forces of the Imperium when they came to her asking for the eye of night.{{Fn|7}} ===Appearance=== Moriana appeared to Honsou as a wizened old woman whose eyes had been removed centuries earlier.{{Fn|1}} ===Trivia=== {{Trivia}} [[Battlefleet Gothic: Armada (Video Game)]] strongly suggests that the figure who caused Abaddon to attempt the capture of the Blackstone Fortresses was actually the [[C'tan]] [[Mephet'ran]], the Deceiver, disguising himself as Moriana. This calls into question whether this was an isolated incident or if Moriana has always been a puppet of Mephet'ran;{{Fn|4}} notably, characters such as Iskandar Khayon claim that Moriana is a generally dividing and deceitful influence.{{Fn|3}} ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Iron Warrior (Novella)]], Chapter One *{{Endn|2}}: [[Inquisitor: The Thorians]], pg. 7 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Black Legion (Novel)]], Chapters 4-5 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Battlefleet Gothic: Armada (Video Game)]] *{{Endn|5}}: [[The End and the Death: Volume I (Novel)]] - 4:i *{{Endn|6}}: [[The End and the Death: Volume III (Novel)]] - 9:xiii *{{Endn|7}}: [[Eye of Night (Audio Drama)]] [[Category:Characters (Chaos Human)]] [[Category:Characters (Human Psykers)]] [[Category:Characters (Inquisition)]] [[Category:Iron Warriors (Novel Series)]]

Morr.wikitext:
{{DrukhariPortal}}
'''Morr''' is a [[Dark Eldar]] [[Incubus]] who has faithfully and loyally served the [[Kabal of the Realm Eternal]] for many generations, upholding the Silent Brotherhoods oaths to his [[Archon]].{{Fn|1b}}

==History==
[[Image:Morr.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Morr{{Fn|2i}}]]
Morr was an imposing and ruthless warrior, efficiently carrying out [[Kraillach]]'s orders without question.{{Fn|1a}} He led the operation planned by [[Nyos Yllithian]] of the [[Kabal of the White Flames]] to steal a [[Worldsinger]] from the maiden world of [[Lileathanir]] so her torture would resurrect the infamous [[El'uriaq]].{{Fn|1b}} 

However his master Kraillach had become increasingly paranoid and weak following a battle with [[Xelian]] of the [[Kabal of the Blades of Desire]], forcing Morr to assume much of the day-to-day management of the Realm Eternal. Despite this, Morr only turned on his master when he discovered that El'Uriaq had corrupted Kraillach, possessing his body with a [[Daemon]]. Morr freed his master from the Daemon's grip by striking down Kraillach.{{Fn|1c}} 

Breaking the oaths of the Silent Brotherhood, Morr vanished after killing his master, followed by the [[Harlequin]] [[Motley]].{{Fn|1c}} While fleeing through the sewers of Commorragh, a [[Dysjunction]] begins to visibly effect the city and the city descended into chaos. The duo narrowly escaped through a [[Webway]] gate moments before it was destroyed by the dysjunction.{{Fn|2a}} Moved by guilt for what he had done, Morr resolved to seek judgement at the Shrine of [[Arhra]].{{Fn|2b}} Through navigating a memory-shard of Morr's homeworld, the duo were able to recent the Shrine of Arhra.{{Fn|2c}}

At the Shrine, Morr was challenged by another Incubus and defeated this rival of the duel. However this was still not enough to pay for his crimes, and the other Incubui reveal they intend to kill him before he can reach the Shrine Hierarchs.{{Fn|2d}} Morr and Motley were able to overcome all the enemies set before them before reaching the main hall and being confronted by [[Drazhar]]. Morr was defeated, but Drazhar surprisingly spared his life much to the anger of the Hierarchs, who dispatched more Incubi to kill him. Motley and Morr were able to flee once more.{{Fn|2f}}

Taken prisoner by the [[Tzeentch]]ian-corrupted [[Warlock]] [[Caraeis]], Motley and Morr were able to escape thanks to the aid of the Harlequin's kin.{{Fn|2f}} Arriving on the now-frozen [[Exodite World]] of [[Lileathanir]] and Motley revealed that Morr was the key to calming its enraged [[World Spirit]], which was thrown into fury by the Dark Eldar capture of the [[World Singer]].{{Fn|2g}} Caraeis arrived to stop Morr, but was killed by the [[Dire Avengers]] [[Exarch]] [[Aiosa]] and Morr was able to sacrifice himself to merge with the World Spirit and stop the planet's destruction. This in turn caused the devastating Dysjunction in Commorragh to subside.{{Fn|2h}}

{{CrimsonSlaughterPortal}}

'''Mortis Metalikus''' is the name given to a [[Helbrute]] of the [[Crimson Slaughter]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
Formerly known as '''Sevarion Kranon''', he was the birth brother of [[Sevastus Kranon]], [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Crimson Sabres]].  Refusing to give in to the bloodthirst that possessed his fellow [[Battle-Brother]]s during the massacre of [[Umidia]], Sevarion was imprisoned by his brother for his disobedience.  However, the curse his entire Chapter experienced from [[Khorne]] eventually drove the once noble soul completely mad during his confinement.  Eventually, Sevarion was imprisoned into the cold shell of a Hellbrute.  He is now consumed by murderous rage and grotesquely corrupted by the powers of [[Chaos]].{{Fn|1}}

Mortis Metalikus would later take part in the [[Battle for Bane's Landing]] and would claim the lives of two [[Ravenwing]] marines and one [[Deathwing]] [[Terminator]] before being destroyed in a duel with [[Librarian]] [[Turmiel]] and Battle-Brother [[Heskia]].  He accepted and welcomed death.{{Fn|3}}

Morven.wikitext:
{{CrimsonFistsPortal}}
'''Venerable {{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Venerable Dreadnought|Dreadnought]] in the [[Crimson Fists]] [[Chapter]], who aided his [[Battle Brother]]s in fighting the vast [[Ork]] horde which attacked them shortly after the [[Great Rift]]'s creation. However, the Chapter was still suffering from the wounds and losses they had suffered in their recent victorious battle with the [[Daemon Prince]] [[Rhaxor]] and weeks later they began to be overwhelmed by the Orks. Seeing that they had no chance of surviving on their own, [[Chapter Master]] [[Pedro Kantor]] sent out a plea for aid, as now only a few scattered groups of Crimson Fists remained. Kantor commanded one of the largest groups of Crimson Fists remaining and shortly after he sent out his message, they began to be pursued by a horde of Orks led by [[Warboss]] [[Ripfist Hakmaw]]. Kantor's group was vastly outnumbered and was forced to constantly retreat until they reached '''New Rynn City''' and could no longer escape from the Warboss. In the battle that followed, the Orks swarmed the Crimson Fists' position and {{PAGENAME}} charged at a [[Morkanaut]] which had killed several of his Battle Brothers. Though he was able to grievously damage the Ork war engine single handily, it retaliated by crushing {{PAGENAME}} to death with its massive [[power claw]].{{Fn|1}}

(As Abbess) |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Adepta Sororitas]] ***[[Order of the Argent Shroud]] **[[High Lords of Terra]] |Notes = }} '''Morvenn Vahl''' is the current [[Abbess of the Adepta Sororitas]] and a [[High Lord of Terra]].{{Fn|1}} ===Biography=== ====Promotion to Abbess==== Originally a [[Celestian]] of the [[Order of the Argent Shroud]], at the start of the [[Indomitus Crusade]] she was placed in her position by the [[Ecclesiarch]] to refill the [[Sabrina|previously vacant]] position of [[Abbess of the Adepta Sororitas|Abbess]] in a bid to improve morale. She was one of the youngest Abbess' ever to hold the position. The scheming clergy of the [[Adeptus Ministorum]] sought to control the new Abbess by making sure she was politically inexperienced and without allies.{{Fn|8}} Vahl was not even consulted and only found out about her promotion when Ecclesiarchy delegates arrived to inform her while she was waging the [[Reskgard Purgation]].{{Fn|3}} Vahl stunned all present by not immediately accepting the position, but instead declaring she would need a period of prayer to consider. Entering her Mission's shrine to [[Saint Silvana]] for three days, when she emerged, she accepted the promotion to Abbess. She again shocked all present by immediately demanding someone fill her current position before making for Terra, ignoring the many planned days of celebration and ritual to mark the occasion.{{Fn|3}} At some point after her promotion, she was appointed to a [[High Lord of Terra]] by [[Roboute Guilliman]].{{Fn|8}} ====Commander of the Adepta Sororitas==== [[Image:VahlArt.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|2}}]] After arriving at [[Terra]], Vahl proved far more difficult to control than the Ecclesiarch had initially thought. Continuing to wear full battle armour even in the presence of members of the [[Holy Synod]], her pitiless and baroque nature intimidated many of the [[Cardinal]]s and Ministorum bureaucrats. Her initial focus was to re-establish contact with as many Orders as possible in the wake of the [[Great Rift]] and nearly all of her work was focused around strictly military matters. Even after being promoted to a [[High Lord of Terra]] by [[Roboute Guilliman]] himself Vahl showed little interest in a political career and instead sought to continue her role as a military commander.{{Fn|3}} To that end, few were surprised when she appointed herself commander of the [[Crusade]] against the traitorous traitor worlds of the [[Philosopher's Belt]]. Leading forces from every major Order, Vahl led by example and to the field personally to defeat the traitors. During these exploits she mostly ignored the many slew of [[General]]s, [[Governor]]s, and [[Admiral]]s that clamored for her attention and instead left such matters to her [[Orders Dialogus]] and [[Orders Famulous]] staffers.{{Fn|3}} ====Feat of Arms==== Unlike her predecessors she continues to lead her Sisters from the frontlines. The Ecclesiarch had initially hoped Vahl would be an easy pawn, to no avail.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2}}{{Fn|3}} One of her first missions after her appointment to Abbess was to relieve [[Ophelia VII]] [[Ophelian Crusade|as it was under attack from the Night Lords]] warlord [[Kol Rakhul]]. Vahl immediately became frustrated by both the Ecclesiarchy and other High Lords, who sent little aid.{{Fn|6a}} Departing aboard the [[Battlecruiser]] ''[[Lux Dominus]]'', her small flotilla was immediately set upon by Night Lords when it entered the Ophelia System. During the fighting, the Captain of the ''Lux Dominus'' overlords his own vessels reactor to prevent its capture, forcing Vahl and her troops to crash-land on Ophelia VII.{{Fn|6b}} Battling through swathes of [[Cultist]]s and [[Chaos Space Marine]]s, Vahl was able to link up with [[Black Templars]] forces under [[Marshal (Black Templars)|Marshal]] [[Montford]] and [[Castellan (Black Templars)|Castellan]] [[Aymar Tancret]]. While initially planning for a direct assault on Kol Rakhul's stronghold, Vahl frustrates the Templars by diverting her own forces to instead launch a subterranean assault in order to rescue a group of remaining [[Battle Sister]]s, pilgrims, and the relic of [[Saint Athenasia]] near a cathedral.{{Fn|6c}} Leading her [[Celestian]]s, the Sisters navigated the desecrated catacombs beneath Ophelia VII before emerging at the cathedral to defeat a [[Heldrake]]. Vahl is shaken when Cultists kill Sister [[Aleyna]], who had earlier exhibited miraculous abilities.{{Fn|6d}} Vahl is nonetheless able to organize the defenses of [[Convent Sanctorum]] for a final stand against the Chaos hordes. In the ensuing battle, she personally faces down Kol Rakhul. While badly wounded in the battle, she is able to impale the vengeful Chaos Lord with her lance.{{Fn|6e}} In the aftermath, she oversaw the rituals for the fallen before returning to Terra to confront the High Lords with the severed head of Kol Rakhul in hand. The campaign proved decisive in earning the respect of the [[Senatorum Imperialis]].{{Fn|6f}} She later took part in the [[Indomitus Crusade Fleet Secundus]]' [[Battle Group Erastus (Fleet Secundus)|Battle Group Erastus]] where joined with [[Marshal (Black Templars)|Marshal]] [[Gideon (Black Templars)|Gideon]], [[Emperor's Champion]], and [[Baron]] [[Munstis]] and his [[Imperial Knights]] of [[House Fidelitor]] she defeated the [[Witch-Empress]] and her daemonic patrons on [[Vastoros]].{{Fn|5}} One of her most recent campaigns was that in [[Charadon Campaign|Charadon]], where she led [[Battle Group Tarsus]] and defeated the forces of the [[Black Legion]] [[Lord Discordant]] [[Akhorath Zeid]].{{Fn|4}} ===Wargear=== In battle, Morvenn Vahl wields the relic [[Power Spear]] ''[[Lance of Illumination‎]]'', which was gifted to her by the [[Adeptus Custodes]], as well as the [[Paragon Warsuit]] ''[[Purgator Mirabilis]]''.{{Fn|1}} ===Images=== File:VahlMini.jpg|Morvenn Vahl miniature{{Fn|1}} File:JoytoyMorvenn.jpg|Morvenn Vahl Joytoy figure{{Fn|7}} ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/2021/05/04/warhammer-fest-online-day-2-warhammer-40000/ Warhammer Community: Warhammer Fest Online: Day 2 – Warhammer 40,000 (Posted on 5/4/2021)] ''(Last accessed 5/4/2021)'' *{{Endn|2}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/2021/05/10/this-high-lord-of-terra-prefers-the-battlefield-to-the-boardroom/ Warhammer Community: This High Lord of Terra Prefers the Battlefield to the Boardroom (posted May 10 2021)] ''(last accessed 5/10/2021)'' *{{Endn|3}}: [[Codex: Adepta Sororitas (9th Edition)]], pgs. 14-15 *{{Endn|4}}: [[War Zone Charadon - Act II: The Book of Fire]], pgs. 36-37 *{{Endn|5}}: [[Codex: Black Templars (9th Edition)]], pg. 25 - ''Heimdel Crusade'' *{{Endn|6}}: [[Morvenn Vahl: Spear of Faith (Novel)]] cover **{{Endn|6a}}: Chapter I **{{Endn|6b}}: Chapter X **{{Endn|6c}}: Chapters XII-XIII **{{Endn|6d}}: Chapters XXIV-XXV **{{Endn|6e}}: Chapter XXXIV **{{Endn|6f}}: Chapter XXXVI *{{Endn|7}}: [https://www.joytoy.com/products/adepta-sororitas-abbess-sanctorum-morvenn-vahl Joytoy Morvenn Vahl] ''(last accessed 21 July 2024)'' *{{Endn|8}}: [[Codex: Adepta Sororitas (10th Edition)]], pgs. 24-25 {{SoBUnits}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Vahl, Morvenn}} [[Category:Characters (Adepta Sororitas)]] [[Category:Characters (High Lords of Terra)]] [[Category:Characters (Human)]] [[Category:Characters (Indomitus Crusade)]]

[[Chaplain]] '''Mulvarius''' served in the [[Ultramarines]] [[3rd Company (Ultramarines)|Third Company]] under [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Ardias|Jehnnus Ardias]]. The Company was stationed aboard the [[Imperial Navy|Imperial Navy's]] [[Emperor Class Battleship]] the ''[[Enduring Blade]]''{{Fn|1a}} (the flagship of [[Battlefleet Ultima Primus]]) when it received a request for aid from the planet [[Dolumar IV]], which was being attacked by the [[Tau]].{{Fn|1b}} Once there, Mulvarius led his Brothers in battle prayers as they prepared to battle the Tau, who had managed to board the ''Enduring Blade'', but [[Epistolary]] [[Delpheus]], plagued by visions that a more powerful enemy would show itself aboard the ship, managed to convince his old friend Ardias that they needed to save their strength and avoid fighting the Tau. Ardias was convinced by Delpheus and told his company to stay where they were; he let Captain [[Mito]] and the [[Raptors (Chapter)|Raptors]] [[Chapter|Chapter's]] [[5th Company (Raptors)|Fifth Company]], who are also stationed aboard the ''Enduring Blade'', deal with the Tau.{{Fn|1a}}

This would prove fortunate as the [[heretic]] [[Meyloch Severus]], [[Planetary Governor]] of Dolumar IV, would complete a [[Chaos]] ritual that summoned a warhost aboard the ''Enduring Blade'' that soon overran the doomed ship.{{Fn|1c}} It isn't known if Mulvarius survived to evacuate the ship{{Fn|1d}} with Ardias and his [[Space Marine Company|Company]] before it was destroyed{{Fn|1e}} or take part in the ensuing battle when the Chaos warhost engulfed Dolumar IV{{Fn|1f}} before its eventual destruction by [[Exterminatus]].{{Fn|1g}}

Murdin Eyclone.wikitext:
{{ChaosPortal}}
[[Image:Murdin-Eyclone.jpg|350px|thumb|right|Murdin Eyclone{{Fn|2}}]]
'''Murdin Eyclone''' was a servant of [[Chaos]], who had operated in and around the [[Helican]] Subsector. Described as a "facilitator", Eyclone hired out his services to any [[Chaos cult]] who needed him.{{Fn|1a}} Eyclone was a [[psyker]], whose powers allowed him to control others, and to wipe memories.

[[Inquisitor]] [[Gregor Eisenhorn]] first encountered Eyeclone working as a gun-for-hire on the frozen world of [[Hox]], where he was doing mercenary work for a small Chaos cult. Eyeclone managed to escape Eisenhorn, who, over the next year, pursued him through two hive worlds until eventually meeting again on a world called [[Tornish]]. Cutting through the local gang that Eyeclone had employed to protect him, with the help of a traitor ganger named [[Lores Vibben]], Eisenhorn came close to cornering Eyeclone, who then sicced an [[ork]] gladiator named '''Gosspit''' on the Inquisitor, giving himself the time he needed to escape as Eisenhorn and Vibben fought the ork, then had to burn away any potential ork spores from the area.{{Fn|3}}

Eyeclone eluded Eisenhorn for a further five years, becoming an incredibly notorius criminal over the period. Although Eisenhorn had other duties, he continued to obsess over Eyeclone, and Eyeclone knew this. In 240.[[M41]], Eyeclone embedded a [[daemon]] within a Warp cipher protecting an astropathic communique that Eisenhorn's astropath [[Krintos]] had intercepted and was attempting to decode. Before the daemon was able to fully possess Krintos, he managed to tell Eisenhorn that Eyeclone was on the planet [[Hubris]].{{Fn|3}}

Eyeclone was on Hubris attempting to murder the entire population of the planet, who were cryogenically frozen, in a ritual intended to empower [[Pontius Glaw]]{{Fn|1b}}. The scheme was abandoned at the last minute, which coincided with Eisenhorn's arrival. Despite the death of Vibben, and the multitude of deaths of those roused from cryosleep too early by Eyclone, Eisenhorn cornered Eyclone on the roof, and, having ensured [[Midas Betancore]] had dealt with his men, killed him{{Fn|1c}}. Eyclone's [[Gifts of Chaos|gifted]] defence mechanism, that of an extending metallic worm hidden under his fingernail, was destroyed by Eisenhorn, [[Uber Aemos]] and [[Godwyn Fischig]].{{Fn|1a}}

N'Kari.wikitext:
{{Character |Portal ={{SlaaneshPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image = |Caption = |Title = |Homeworld = |Birth = |Active Period = |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species ='' '' *[[Human]]
(Former) *[[Daemon]] |Type =[[Daemon Prince]]{{Fn|Conflicting Sources}} |Gender = |Relatives = |Occupation = |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Chaos]] **[[Slaanesh]] |Notes = }} '''N'Kari''' is a powerful [[Daemon]] of [[Slaanesh]].{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|Conflicting sources}} ===History=== As a mortal, N'Kari was born on an isolated, backwater world which had been trapped in the centre of a violent [[Warp Storm|warp storm]] for millennia; incidentally, this was the same backwater world as the mortal who would become the Daemon Prince [[Bubonicus (Character)|Bubonicus]]. The Powers of [[Chaos]] had repeatedly attempted to conquer this planet, but had been foiled by the uncorrupted peoples of the world. N'Kari rose to prominence during one of the Chaos Powers' many attempts to conquer the planet. He proved himself a dedicated follower of Slaanesh in countless battles - and the debauched and disgusting revelries that followed them - and was rewarded by Slaanesh with the gift of Daemonhood. Along with [[Doombreed]], he was one of the two Daemon Princes that fought against the [[Emperor of Mankind|Emperor]] when he boarded [[Horus|Horus's]] [[Battle Barge|battle barge]], the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]'', and he continues to serve his daemonic master to this day.{{Fn|1}} During the [[Horus Heresy]], N'Kari was one of many [[Daemon]]s summoned by [[Erebus]], [[First Chaplain]] of the [[Word Bearers]], by a dark ritual conducted during the [[Battle of Calth]].{{Fn|4}} N'Kari later reappeared at [[Fulgrim]]'s side as his consort, among a crowd of onlookers, which enganged in general debauchery. When Fulgrim refused [[Lorgar|Lorgar's]] demand to come with him to [[Ullanor]] and rejoin Horus's war, N'kari joined Fulgrim in attacking the [[Word Bearers]]. However, Fulgrim was bound by [[Zardu Layak]] after he uttered the Daemon's [[True Name]] and forced to comply. N'Kari refused to leave Fulgrim's side, and accompanied him back to Ullanor and then the [[Siege of Terra]].{{Fn|6c}} N'Kari was later among the [[Greater Daemons]] summoned into [[Realspace]] by the [[Thousand Sons]], during the [[Siege of Terra]]{{Fn|7a}}. After the [[Lion's Gate Spaceport]] fell to the [[Traitor]]s, the Daemons were unleashed to destroy the [[Imperial Palace]]'s [[Colossi Gate]]{{Fn|7b}}. While they succeeded in tearing down the Gate's outer defenses, the Daemons were destroyed by the [[White Scars]]' [[Stormseers]] and the [[Adeptus Custodes]], before they could complete their task.{{Fn|7c}} At some point, N'Kari battled the [[Eldar]] [[Phoenix Lord]] [[Asurmen]]. The mighty Daemon managed to slay the warrior, but in a rage the fellow Phoenix Lord of the [[Shining Spears]], [[Drastanta]], defeated N'Kari with his [[Celestial Lance]], sending him back to the [[Warp]].{{Fn|5}} During the [[Gheistos Cataclysm]] in [[M41]], N'kari arrived leading an army of [[Fiend]]s and [[Daemonette]]s. His arrival marked the reaching of an alliance between [[Nurgle]] and [[Slaanesh]].{{Fn|2}} N'Kari is an infamous foe of [[Eldrad Ulthran]], and has sought to trap his soul on several occasions.{{Fn|8}} ====Craftworld Malan'tai==== In 800.M41, N'Kari and his [[Daemon]] followers found the derelict [[Craftworld]] [[Malan'tai]] and stalked its ruined halls for hidden caches of [[spirit stone]]s to feed upon. For each spirit stone N'Kari devoured he grew more powerful, and by the time a [[Grey Knight]]s strike force responded to a dire vision by their [[Prognosticar]]s and arrived at the Craftworld, N'Kari had grown in strength tenfold.{{Fn|3}} The Grey Knights purged their way through the ruined halls of Malan'tai, led by [[Grey Knights Brother-Captain|Brother-Captain]] [[Pelenas]] and accompained by as many [[Purifier]]s as possible. Any and all Daemons standing before them were cut down, until the Grey Knight strike force cornered N'Kari in the despoiled [[Dome of Crystal Seers]]. A fierce battle ensued, wherein a dozen Purifiers were slain and Pelenas was struck down. But before the Keeper of Secrets could strike the killing blow against the Captain, [[Justicar]] [[Anval Thawn]] threw himself in front of Pelenas. With N'Kari's spear stuck deep in Thawn's flesh, the surviving Purifiers had enough of a respite to complete the ritual of [[Twelve Bloody Swords]] and successfully drain N'Kari of his stolen power, opening him up to be defeated by Pelenas.{{Fn|3}} ===Appearance=== N'Kari is described as having the lower body of a serpent, much like the [[Daemon Primarch]] [[Fulgrim]]. However, the comparisons end there, as N'Kari is a grotesque obese creature that repulses even the [[Word Bearers]]. In combat, N'Kari will transform itself into a more muscled and lithe form.{{Fn|6b}} ===Trivia=== {{trivia}} N'Kari is also a major antagonist of [[William King|William King's]] '''Warhammer Fantasy''' novel trilogy focusing on the High Elf twins Tyrion and Teclis, and is a playable character in the video game '''Total War: Warhammer III'''. ==== Warhammer World within the 40K Galaxy ==== Although it is implied that N'kari, [[Bubonicus_(Character)|Bubonicus]] and [[Flamefist]] all originate from the same planet and this is the [[https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Warhammer_world| Warhammer World]], it is not specified exactly in this way. [[Bubonicus_(Character)|Bubonicus]] and [[Flamefist]] are introduced in [[Realm of Chaos: The Lost and the Damned]] as Warhammer Fantasy Chaos Champions that successfully ascended to become [[Daemon Prince|Daemon Princes]]. (pgs. 121-126 - ''Chaos Warbands'') Like numerous other daemon characters, a daemon named "N'Kari" exists within both Warhammer Fantasy and Warhammer 40,000. [[Realm of Chaos: The Lost and the Damned]] also specifically mentions ''"The Warhammer World is bound by storms of magic so that it remains isolated from the other worlds of the human galaxy."'' (pg. 77 - ''Chaos Monoliths'') The links to the Warhammer World is more subtly implied for N'Kari in [[Codex: Chaos (2nd Edition)]] ''"N'Kari was born on an isolated, backward world which has been trapped at the centre of a violent warp storm for millennia. The Chaos powers have repeatedly attempted to conqueor this planet, but have so far been foiled by the uncorrupted peoples of the world. N'kari rose to prominence during one of the Chaos Powers' many attempts to conquer the planet"''.{{Fn|1}} Bubonicus is also mentioned in [[Codex: Chaos (2nd Edition)]] as ''"formerly a mortal Champion of Nurgle on one of the myriad lost worlds in the galaxy"'' (p. 131). [[Codex: Chaos (2nd Edition)]] does not specifically state Bubonicus and N'kari originate from the same planet. ==={{Endn|Conflicting sources}}=== N'Kari has been referred to as both a [[Daemon Prince]]{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|6a}} or a [[Keeper of Secrets]]{{Fn|3}}, depending on the source. ===See Also=== * [https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/N'Kari N'Kari in Warhammer Fantasy] ===Sources=== {{cite}} *{{Endn|1}}: [[Codex: Chaos (2nd Edition)]], pg.140 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Battle Missions]], pg. 17 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Codex: Grey Knights (5th Edition)]], pg. 14 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Know No Fear (Novel)]], ''Ushkul//Thu'', Chapter Two, pgs. 345-347 *{{Endn|5}}: [[Iyanden: A Codex: Eldar Supplement]] (E-Book), pg. 83 *6: [[Slaves to Darkness (Novel)]] **{{Endn|6a}}: ''Dramatis Personae'' **{{Endn|6b}}: Chapter 12 **{{Endn|6c}}: Chapter 14 *7: [[Saturnine (Novel)]] **{{Endn|7a}}: Part 1 - Chapter 5 **{{Endn|7b}}: Part 2 - Chapter 2 **{{Endn|7c}}: Part 3 - Chapter 2 *{{Endn|8}}: [[Rise of the Ynnari: Wild Rider (Novel)]] - Prologue

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a member of the [[White Scars]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]]. A [[Stormseer]] of considerable power, he was second only to [[Targutai Yesugei]]. Following Yesugei's death in the [[Battle of Catallus]], Naranbaatar became Chief Stormseer.{{Fn|1}} 

During the [[Siege of Terra]], Naranbaatar was one of the senior White Scars officers at the [[Colossi Gate]]. During the battle, Naranbaatar and his Stormseers were able to fend off a psychic assault by [[Ahriman]] and the [[Order of Ruin]].{{Fn|2}} During Jaghatai Khan's great counterattack to retake the [[Lion's Gate Spaceport]], Naranbaatar took part in the central thrust and led his Stormseers once more.  However after sensing the location of [[Mortarion]] he became separated from Jaghatai Khan and was badly wounded in the fighting. His dying body was discovered by [[Jangsai Khan]], but the Chief Stormseer instead urged the [[Newblood]] Captain to hurry on and help the Great Khan in his battle against [[Mortarion]]. He passed shortly after.{{Fn|3}}

'''Narvo Quin, the Pilgrim,''' is an [[Emperor's Children]] [[Chaos Space Marine]] who serves in the [[12th Millennial]], under the command of [[Savona]].{{Fn|1a}} 

===Biography===
He was originally born on [[Terra]] and during the [[Great Crusade]], Quin was among the [[Emperor's Children]] that [[Fulgrim]] led to victory on [[Byzas]].{{Fn|1b}} Within his legion, he was well known for his ambition and martial prowess.{{Fn|2}} However, [[Fabius Bile]] considered Quin to be a blunt object, who was a brutal tactician with little patience and less wisdom. This changed when the [[Horus Heresy]] began;{{Fn|1b}} at this point, Quin held the rank of Veteran-Tesserarius in the [[5th Company (Emperor's Children)|5th Company]] of the [[7th Millennial]]'s Battalion II. He distinguished himself during the [[Battle of Isstvan III]], killing at least two dozen "notable" loyalists.{{Fn|2}}

Quin and his squad were deployed at the Kesh Rift Salient during the [[Dropsite Massacre]]. His force was overrun during a massive [[Iron Hand]] counter-attack, and Quin was torn apart by [[Gabriel Santar]] in personal combat.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|2}} Loyalist records generally assumed that he had been killed.{{Fn|2}}

After the battle, Bile would find Quin's remains and, for reasons known only to himself, he brought Quin back to life. Quin was not thankful for this, however, but Bile later noted that following his rebirth Quin became more thoughtful and considered. Quin then spent time reforging himself and the [[Power Axe]] [[Fulgrim]] had gifted to him, as the war against the Imperium continued.{{Fn|1b}} When the Heresy ended, Fulgrim continued to lead the Emperor's Children for a time, until he abandoned them after [[Battle of Thessala|Thessala]] to purse his own desires. Quin knew the Legion would splinter without the Daemon Primarch's leadership to bind them together and began a pilgrimage to find Fulgrim.{{Fn|1c}} Though he realized it was a foolish task, no other high ranking member of the Emperor's Children sought to try and as a Terran-born Legionary he felt he was worthy of succeeding.{{Fn|1d}} His journey eventually led him to [[Callax]], where he arrived in time to save [[Fabius Bile]]'s daughter [[Melusine]], from being killed by a horde of [[Daemon]]s. She had sought to prove worthy enough to convince Fulgrim to help her father, but it was Quin's interference that drew the Daemon Primarch out.{{Fn|1d}}

With his journey finally at an end, Quin attempted to sway Fulgrim to retake control of the Emperor's Children, but the Daemon Primarch had no interest. After only mere moments of talking to Fulgrim, the Daemon Primarch used his powers to evict from and sent him casting away elsewhere.{{Fn|1c}} Afterwards the Emperor's Children splintered into [[Chaos Warband|Warband]]s, and Quin's began being sought after by Brothers who wanted to learn where Fulgrim secretly dwelled. He refused to tell them, however, and was forced to kill those who would not take no for an answer. After he lost count of the number of Emperor's Children he was forced to kill, Quin's sense of duty, and the full weight of what he had been forced to do, led him to seek refuge on an unnamed [[Daemon World]].{{Fn|1d}} 

He would remain there for sometime, and was believed to be dead, until Fabius Bile later learned of Quin's location and asked for his aid in finding Fulgrim. At that time, Bile was being hunted by the [[Coven of the Thirteen Scars]] and needed Fulgrim's help if he was to survive his war with the [[Haemonculi]]. Quin refused at first, but was suddenly visited by [[Melusine]]. Due to now being a creature of the [[Warp]], she was able to appear to Quin while he was alone and convinced him to aid Bile. Quin relented and informed Bile he would lead the way to Fulgrim's location, without explaining why he had changed his mind.{{Fn|1b}}

Once Bile met with the Daemon Primarch and secured his aid{{Fn|1e}}, he convinced Quin to accompany him to his main base of operations on [[Belial IV]]. Once there, Bile learned the Coven was moving to invade the world and he met with the [[Chaos Lords]] Fulgrim had sent to aid him. Due to various reasons, however, they were reluctant to do so, until Quin intervened on Bile's behalf. His threatening words, stating that Fulgrim and Slaanesh would view those that did not help as cowards{{Fn|1f}}, led the Chaos Lords to agree to help Bile. After the meeting, Quin decided to leave Belial IV but was convinced to stay by [[Savona]], the current commander of the [[12th Millennial]]. He became intrigued by her, as she was a non-[[Chaos Space Marine]] leading a Warband, and wanted to see how she would fare in the coming battle.{{Fn|1d}} When the Coven of the Thirteen Scar finally [[Battle of Belial IV|invaded Belial IV]]. Savona and Quin fought side by side, against the unending hordes of the Haemonculi's creatures. Eventually, like they had known it would, the battle turned against Bile's forces and Savona gave the order for the 12th Millennial to escape. She asked Quin what he planned on doing and he replied that he was tired of hiding. Quin then said he sought something new and joined the 12th Millennial, as they evacuated from Belial IV.{{Fn|1a}}

{{QuoteBox |quote = '''''"Men crave food. They crave flesh, they crave power. We are not men, the [[Emperor of Mankind|Emperor's]] Angels. His [[Space Marines]] crave honour, they crave retribution, they crave justice. We are not angels. We are the blood-sons of [[Sanguinius]]. We crave only violence, bloodshed. [[Cretacia]] |Birth =c. [[M30]], [[Terra]] |Active Period =[[M30]] - ???.[[M31]] |Death =???.[[M31]] |Cause of Death =Disappearance at the edge of the [[Cretacia]] System{{Fn|7c}} |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Astartes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives =[[Sanguinius]] ("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *[[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Blood Angels]] 5th Company *[[Dominion (Blood Angels)|Dominion]] of the [[Blood Angels]] *[[Chapter Master]] of the [[Flesh Tearers]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Blood Angels]] **[[Flesh Tearers]] |Notes = }} '''Nassir Amit'''{{Fn|3a}}, also known as "the Flesh Tearer", was the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] and [[Dominion (Blood Angels)|Dominion]] of the [[5th Company (Blood Angels Legion)|Fifth Company]] of the [[Blood Angels]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1b}} Following the Heresy, Amit became the first [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Flesh Tearers]].{{Fn|2}} ===Biography=== ====Great Crusade==== Nassir Amit was one of the first members of the IXth Legion, which in time would become known as the '''Revenant Legion''' for their barbaric practices such as consuming their own dead. A scion of a toxic bloodline in [[Boeotia]], he was a quasi-[[Mutant]] that would have been executed by any other Legion. Instead he was reformed into a [[Space Marine]] and took the name Nassir Amit from an ancient Himalayan play. After his ascension he fully took part in the brutal practices of his Legion, executing captured enemy soldiers and consuming them alongside his fallen brothers.{{Fn|9b}} All of this changed with the arrival of [[Sanguinius]], who pledged himself to his sons regardless of what path they may take. Under Sanguinius' guidance, the Revenant Legion was reborn into the noble Blood Angels and abandoned its barbaric practices. However Nassir continued to display much of his Legion's former behavior, becoming a famed champion in the gladiator-pits of the [[World Eaters]]. When his chain-brother [[Kargos Bloodspitter]] was challenged to a fight to the death by two World Eaters champions, Nassir defended his brother and struck down his foes in the presence of Sanguinius and [[Angron]]. Sanguinius allowed the bout to take place, but expressed disappointment with Nassir in the aftermath and instructed him to eat the brains of the two World Eaters he had slain. The act secretly shamed Nassir.{{Fn|9b}} Amit and the Fifth Company partook in the joint Blood Angels/[[Luna Wolves]] assault on the [[Nephilim]] on [[Melchior]].{{Fn|1c}} Later, Amit accompanied his [[Primarch]] [[Sanguinius]], [[First Captain]] [[Raldoron]], and Captain [[Thoros]] to the [[Council of Nikaea]], where Amit was commanded to stand sentinel in the Great Angel's quarters. When the [[Emperor of Mankind]] issued the Edict of Nikaea, Amit, who was staunchly pro-[[Librarian]], suspected that it was because Sanguinius feared that Amit would try to argue with the Emperor. When Raldoron returned to the Blood Angels quarters, Amit argued with Raldoron that commanding the Librarians to never again use their powers was a mistake, and expressed concerned about how they were to be reintegrated. Sanguinius entered and assured Amit that the Librarians still be welcomed in the Blood Angels ranks, but that the Emperor's word was law, and the Edict of Nikaea was to be followed.{{Fn|1a}} At some point during the [[Great Crusade]], Nassmir Amit fought [[Kharn]] of the [[World Eaters]] on a desert planet that both their Legions had conquered in a joint action. Both fighters were badly wounded in a brutal duel in a trench using axes and cleavers.{{Fn|4}} ====Heresy==== Amit and the Fifth Company later joined the joint Blood Angels/[[Alpha Legion]] operation in the [[Kayvas Belt]] fighting the [[Ork]]s.{{Fn|1b}} Following the campaign, Amit and the Fifth accompanied the rest of the Blood Angels Legion in their campaign in the [[Signus Cluster]]. After rescuing [[Squad Cassiel]] on [[Holst]] from [[Chaos|strange hostiles]],{{fn|1d}} Amit began to have concerns that the Blood Angels had been lead into a trap. Having been aware that Raldoron's adjutant, [[Mkani Kano]], had been seeking out his former brothers in the [[Librarius (Fortress-monastery)|Librarius]], Amit approached the former Librarian and offered to help him.{{fn|1e}} After the ''[[Red Tear]]'' had crashed on [[Signus Prime]] and the ''[[Dark Page]]'' under [[Chaplain]] [[Tanus Kreed]] of the [[Word Bearers]] fled, Sanguinius called a meeting of the [[Council of Angels]], Amit finally spoke what he had feared: [[Warmaster]] [[Horus Lupercal]] had lead the Blood Angels into a trap. The words had barely left his lips when Sanguinius struck Amit in the chest with the pommel of his sword and demanded Amit recant his statement. Though clearly shocked at his Primarch's outburst, Amit stood by his accusation. He was only spared censure when [[Helik Redknife]] of the [[Space Wolves]] revealed that Primarch [[Magnus]] of the [[Thousand Sons]] had violated the Edict of Nikaea.{{fn|1f}} During the [[Battle of Signus Prime]], when Sanguinius was wounded by [[Ka'Bandha]], the Blood Angels fell to the depths of rage, and Amit and some of his warriors succumbed to the [[Red Thirst]]. In the throes of the rage, Amit and his brothers descended upon Redknife and his Wolves, killing them.{{fn|1g}} Following the battle, Amit revealed what he had done to First Captain Raldoron, and submitted himself to punishment. However, [[Azkaellon]], the Commander of the [[Sanguinary Guard]], prevented him, and Raldoron revealed that Azkaellon had already lied to Sanguinius about the Wolves deaths. Amit nearly came to blows with the Guard Commander, but Azkaellon explained that if Sanguinius knew what had happened, he would blame himself and tell [[Leman Russ (Primarch)|Leman Russ]] the truth, risking the bonds between the Legiones Astartes at a time when unity was needed. Amit asked how he was supposed to ease the pain in his heart, and Azkaellon told him that it was the burden he must bear.{{Fn|1h}} [[Image:NassirVsKargos.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Nassir Amit battles [[Kargos Bloodspitter]] during the [[Siege of Terra]]{{Fn|9a}}]] Later, Sanguinius warned Nassir Amit to control his emotions during the [[Battle of Pyrrhan]].{{Fn|5}} During the [[Battle of Beta-Garmon]] Nassir Amit led Blood Angels forces against traitor forces on [[Beta-Garmon II]]'s Nyrcon City.{{Fn|6}} During the [[Siege of Terra]], Nassir Amit took part in the defense of the [[Inner Palace]]. During a defense of a refugee convoy, Nassir met his former chain-brother [[Kargos]] and cut his throat after telling him to simply ''eat shit'', though this failed to kill the World Eater.{{Fn|9a}} Later Nassir was one of the sparse number of defenders at the [[Eternity Gate (Imperial)|Eternity Gate]], holding off a massive Chaos horde. During the battle he again came to blows with Kargos, again telling him to "eat shit" and striking down his former brother.{{Fn|9c}} Following the sealing of the Eternity Gate, Amit wept at the sight of the Angel's wounds at the hand of [[Ka'Bandha]] and [[Angron]] as well as the doom the shutting of the gate meant for Terra.{{Fn|10a}} After the fall of [[Bhab Bastion]], Amit rallied with remaining loyalist officers such as [[Fafnir Rann]], [[Namahi]], [[Azkaellon]], [[Dominion Zephon|Zephon]], [[Satel Aimery]] in the final defense of the Inner Palace under the command of [[Archamus II|Archamus]].{{Fn|10b}} During the fighting, normal space-time began to break down as the [[Warp]] swept across Terra and traitors were able to bypass the sealed [[Eternity Gate (Imperial)|Eternity Gate]] and pour deep into the [[Sanctum Imperialis]]. Amit led resistance to traitor advance at at the Marnix Confluence, just 2km from the Throneroom.{{Fn|11}} Upon sensing the death of Sanguinius, Amit succumbed to the [[Black Rage]] with the rest of his Legion.{{Fn|12a}} He went on a particularly gruesome rampage, massacring large numbers of loyalists until the wave of insanity lifted. He was discovered amid a sea of loyal corpses by the [[Lone Wolf]] [[Odi Sartak]], who had been about to try and stop Amit.{{Fn|12b}} Expressing horror and grief at what he had done, after the defeat of Horus Amit is seen taking part in the funeral service for Sanguinius alongside 500 surviving Blood Angels.{{Fn|12c}} ====Post-Heresy==== Following the Heresy, Amit became Master of a Chapter of the [[Second Founding]], which bore the name "Flesh Tearers" after his own epithet.{{fn|2}} With the death of Sanguinius, Amit and his followers gave into their resentment and hatred, unleashing bloody rampages against the traitors as they retreated from [[Terra]]. He later lead the Flesh Tearers to conquer [[Cretacia]] and take the planet as the Chapter's new homeworld.{{Fn|3b}} Amit became obsessed with Cretacia, believing it to be the manifestation of the Flesh Tearers' own nature, hoping that if he could tame its peaks he could temper the edges of his own fury.{{Fn|8}} Amit's final fate is unknown, as he left Cretacia aboard a ship which vanished at the edge of the [[system]].{{Fn|7b}} Following that, he was never seen alive and his body was never found.{{Fn|7c}} Eventually, his successor, [[Gabriel Seth]], found Amit's helmet in a reliquary aboard an ancient Flesh Tearers vessel, dated to the time before the Second Founding, which had become part of a [[Space Hulk]] that had materialised at the edge of the [[Corythos System]].{{Fn|3c}}{{Fn|7c}} After viewing the images contained in the helmet's cogitators, Seth fell unconscious and the relic was destroyed by [[Harahel]]. Amit's helmet showed Seth a universe of blood which he referred to simply as "the end...".{{Fn|7d}} ===Personality=== Nassir Amit was notorious among the Blood Angels for both his savage and brutally honest nature. The Primarch Sanguinius valued his honest nature, as Amit would always speak the truth, even when others would be stopped by decorum.{{Fn|1a}} His savage aspect in battle was also known, to the point that he was dubbed "the Flesh Tearer" by his battle-brothers. Far from denying the epithet, he embraced it,{{Fn|1b}} arming himself and his brothers in the Fifth Company with custom serrated flaying knives.{{Fn|1c}} Amit did what he believed to be right, even if went against Legion law, having little fear of the [[Warden]]s.{{fn|1e}} ===Wargear=== As Captain of the Legion's Fifth Company, Amit wore a suit of [[Artificer Armour]]{{Fn|1b}}, while in combat he used a custom made [[power sword]]{{Fn|1h}} and [[Astartes Combat Knife|flaying knife]]{{Fn|1g}} with barbed edges, the source of his epithet.{{Fn|1h}} As Chapter Master of the Flesh Tearers, Amit wore a suit of [[Terminator Armour]], utilizing a pair of [[Chainfist]]s with integrated [[Storm Bolter]]s.{{Fn|3c}} Amit was notably the only Chapter Master of the Flesh Tearers to wear Terminator armour; it was believed by [[Chaplain]] [[Appollus]] that Amit's successors saw it as a prison, not allowing them to slake their thirst for bloodshed.{{Fn|7b}} As both Captain and Chapter Master, Amit tended to ignore cosmetic damage to his armour, leaving bullet marks and blade scars as they were, a habit which annoyed his fellow Blood Angels and even some of his fellow Flesh Tearers.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|3c}} Today, Nassir Amit's armor is a prized relic of the Flesh Tearers and is kept in their [[Fortress-Monastery]] on [[Cretacia]]. In [[M42]], shortly before the [[Battle of Cretacia]], the shrine was defiled by the [[Disciples of Rage]] and his armor was worn by the [[First Disciple]].{{Fn|13}} ===See also=== *[[List of Chapter Masters]] *[[List of Founders]] *[[List of Space Marine Captains]] ===Sources=== *1: [[Fear to Tread (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|1a}}: ''Nikaea'' **{{Endn|1b}}: Chapter 2 **{{Endn|1c}}: ''Melchior'' **{{Endn|1d}}: Chapter 8 **{{Endn|1e}}: Chapter 11 **{{Endn|1g}}: Chapter 16 **{{Endn|1h}}: Chapter 20 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Red Fury (Novel)]] — [[Blood Angels: The Second Omnibus]], Chapter 9, pg. 178 *3: [[Flesh of Cretacia (Novella)]]: **{{Endn|3a}}: ''Back Cover'' **{{Endn|3b}}: ''Cover Art'' **{{Endn|3c}}: Chapter One **{{Endn|3d}}: Chapter Four *{{Endn|4}}: [[Virtues of the Sons (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|5}}: [[Ruinstorm (Novel)]], Chapters 8–11 *{{Endn|6}}: [[Titandeath (Novel)]], Chapter 24 *7: [[Hunger (Audio Drama)]] **{{Endn|7a}}: Track 1 **{{Endn|7b}}: Track 3 **{{Endn|7c}}: Track 9 **{{Endn|7d}}: Track 10 *{{Endn|8}}: [[White Dwarf December 2019]], pg. 72 *9: [[Echoes of Eternity (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|9a}}: Chapter 12 **{{Endn|9b}}: Chapters 17-18 **{{Endn|9c}}: Chapter 32 *10: [[The End and the Death: Volume I (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|10a}}: 1:iv **{{Endn|10b}}: 3:vi *{{Endn|11}}: [[The End and the Death: Volume II (Novel)]] - 6:l *12: [[The End and the Death: Volume III (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|12a}}: 9:i **{{Endn|12b}}: 10:xviii **{{Endn|12c}}: Fragments (Agonal) - iii *{{Endn|13}}: [[Wrath of the Lost (Novel)]], Chapter 29 {{DEFAULTSORT:Amit, Nassir}} [[Category:Characters (Blood Angels)]] [[Category:Characters (Flesh Tearers)]] [[Category:Characters (Great Crusade)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[fr:Nassir Amit]]

Nautilacknid.wikitext:
{{KhornePortal}}
The '''Nautilacknid''' is a [[Xenos]] [[Daemon Prince]] of [[Khorne]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
Its unknown species worshiped the [[Blood God]], to the point they butchered each other in his name. Only the Nautilacknid survived his species destruction, due to being the strongest and most savage of them all. As a [[Daemon Prince]], it is swollen with [[Khorne]]'s gifts and has eight eyes and eight arms, with each wielding a different weapon. With these abilities, the Nautilacknid had never once been defeated in battle - until it faced the [[World Eater]] [[Torgax Bloodhair]]. The Daemon Prince found itself outmatched, as Torgax dismembered the Nautilacknid piece by piece. Each of its eyes were put out and each arm was severed by the World Eater, who claimed each of the Daemon Prince's weapons. Finally Torgax decapitated the Nautilacknid, leaving shock and horror etched upon its death-visage.{{Fn|1}}

Navradaran.wikitext:
{{AdeptusCustodesPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' of the [[Ephoroi]] is a member of the [[Adeptus Custodes]], one of the few to leave the [[Imperial Palace]] before the [[Indomitus Crusade]].{{Fn|2a}} Navradaran admired the human spirit{{Fn|2c}} and his counsel taught his friend [[Shield-Captain]] [[Valerian]] to see humans as more than mere irritants.{{Fn|2a}}

==Biography==
[[Image:Navradaran.jpg|thumb|right|300px|{{PAGENAME}} of the [[Ephoroi]]{{Fn|1}}]]
Navradaran was an acquaintance of [[Inquisitor-Lord]] [[Hovash Phaelias]] of the [[Ordo Xenos]], who approached the Custodian during an investigation into [[Rogue Trader]] [[Naaman Vinal]] misusing his [[Warrant of Trade|Letter of Marque]] when he uncovered unusually regular contact between the trader and an [[astropath]] in the personal service of the [[Speaker for the Chartist Captains]]. Phaelias believed something of [[xenos]] origin acquired by Vinal was being smuggled to [[Terra]].{{Fn|1c}}

When Phaelias disappeared shortly after ordering an orbital quarantine, Navradaran apprehended Inquisitor [[Erasmus Crowl]] breaking into an [[Adeptus Arbites]] Precinct-Fortress{{Fn|1a}} in his own investigation of heretical activity beginning at around the same time. He told the Inquisitor to report anything he discovered before the end of [[Sanguinala]] in four days.{{Fn|1b}} Crowl concluded that there was a [[Dark Eldar]] that had been smuggled to Terra and escaped its captors attempting to gain access to the [[Sanctum Imperialis]] through underground passages while all eyes were focussed on the [[Eternity Gate (Imperial)|Eternity Gate]].{{Fn|1d}} Navradaran and four other Custodians accompanied Crowl in the hunt,{{Fn|1e}} impaling the Dark Eldar as it tormented a weakened Crowl.{{Fn|1f}}

===Thirteenth Black Crusade===
During the [[Thirteenth Black Crusade]], Navradaran was often away from the [[Imperial Palace]] as part of [[Captain-General]] [[Trajann Valoris]]' attempt to collect the scattered [[Silent Sisterhood]] to Terra.{{Fn|2d}} While within the Palace, he spoke to [[Shield-Captain|Tribune]] [[Heracleon]] about a dream he had had of [[Valerian]]'s name, and agreed that it was a sign that he was marked for the [[Hetaeron Guard]].{{Fn|2b}}

When the [[Great Rift]], Navradaran was making his way back to Terra aboard the commandeered [[Black Ship]] ''[[Enduring Abundance]]'', stopping at every known or rumoured convent of witch-hunters in the [[subsector]] as well as searching for stray vessels in the [[warp]] such as the ''[[Cadamara]]'' carrying Sister [[Tanau Aleya]]. By the time the ''Enduring Abundance'' returned to Terra, the [[Second Battle of Terra]] was already underway.{{Fn|2d}}

===The Dark City===
Navradaran disappeared after the battle, journeying with [[Erasmus Crowl]] to discover the truth of the conspiracy the Inquisitor had uncovered. The two travel to [[Luna]], discovering that the [[Mechanicum]] is bargaining with the [[Dark Eldar]] to save the [[Golden Throne]].{{Fn|4a}} Together with [[Luce Spinoza]] and an Inquisitorial retinue, Navradaran move into [[Commorragh]] to interrupt the negotiations between [[Fabricator-General]] [[Oud Oudia Raskian]] and [[Archon]] [[Shae-Morvain]] of the [[Kabal of the Still-Living Knife]].{{Fn|4b}} Upon Crowl's exposure of the heretical [[Black Throne]] project, Navradaran lashes out at the Xenos and massacres many of them before helping bring down the entire Xenos complex on top of himself.{{Fn|4c}}

("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *Member of the [[Dark Angels]] (Former) *Leader of the [[Dark Brotherhood (Blackshields)|Dark Brotherhood]] *Member of the [[Knights-Errant]]{{Fn|1a}} *Founding member of the [[Grey Knights]] (Potential) |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Dark Angels]] **[[Knights-Errant]] *[[Blackshields]] **[[Dark Brotherhood (Blackshields)|Dark Brotherhood]] |Notes = }} The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' — also called the '''Nemean Reaver''', the '''Scarred Master''', and the '''Gloaming Slayer''' — was a member of the [[Dark Angels]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]]. He was the '''First Lord''' of a [[Blackshields]] warband called the [[Dark Brotherhood (Blackshields)|Dark Brotherhood]] during the [[Horus Heresy]] before joining the [[Knights-Errant]].{{Fn|1a}} ===Biography=== The Nemean was a [[Terra]]n member of the Dark Angels Legion and a veteran of the [[Third Rangdan Xenocide]].{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}} ===Horus Heresy=== During the Horus Heresy, the Nemean gathered a band of Blackshields who came to be known as the Dark Brotherhood, binding them into a coherent force under his leadership. The Nemean set out to [[Pale Stars campaign (Horus Heresy)|establish an independent empire]] as a haven for the Brotherhood in [[the Pale Stars]]. Operating from the [[Eridayn Cataract]], they set out to cleanse their realm of [[human]] and [[xenos]] [[pirate]]s as well as [[Imperialis Armada]] patrol craft. In late 007.[[M31]], the Nemean led an assault on 771/51-6, executing the master of the human-xenos hybrid clans that had been operating in the region since the [[Age of Strife]].{{Fn|1a}} Soon after, an [[Alpha Legion]] force under Strike Master [[Ijax]] came to the Pale Stars to raise armies for the traitors, promising the ruling houses [[Horus]]' favour if they aided him in purging the Dark Brotherhood. Even as the Alpha Legion sought to provoke the Nemean by deploying their militias on many worlds claimed by the Brotherhood, the Nemean focused his efforts so that the Alpha Legion thousands-strong armies into isolated regions where they would suffer starvation and hazardous conditions for no gain.{{Fn|1a}} In 017008.M31, the Nemean and his Brotherhood came to [[Optera IV]] after receiving a coded [[astropath]]ic message from [[Nathaniel Garro]]. Garro had been sent to recruit the Nemean for the [[Knights-Errant]], his name one of twenty drawn up by [[Malcador the Sigillite|Malcador]] and [[Severian (The Wolf)|Severian]]. The Nemean asked what had become of his [[primarch]], [[Lion El'Jonson]], pressing for an answer even after the Alpha Legion sprung an ambush. Garro told him there was no news, and the Nemean took one look at the chaos of the battle being fought by the Dark Brotherhood, Alpha Legion, and other loyalists who answered Garro's call before nodding his agreement. The Nemean was [[teleport]]ed aboard Garro's ship and returned to Terra.{{Fn|1a}} The Nemean went on to serve Malcador as a Knight-Errant, supposedly fighting and dying on the walls of the [[Imperial Palace]] during the [[Siege of Terra]].{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}} However it is possible he became [[Epimetheus]], as the individual is a Dark Angel who admits to never having a true name.{{Fn|2}} ===Appearance and Wargear=== The Nemean was marred by terrible scars from the Rangdan Xenocide, his face a twisted mass of scar tissue hidden beneath a ragged hood. He wore the '''Kithairon War Plate''', a suit of void-hardened and reputedly impenetrable{{fn|1a}} [[artificer armour]] believed to include elements of a suit of [[power armour]] that predated the [[Imperium]] by several millennia. He also wore an [[iron halo]].{{Fn|1b}} For weaponry, he wielded a '''[[Calibanite Flammbard]]''', a two-handed, flame-edged sword forged by a hidden order of blade-smiths. Alongside this he carried a master-crafted [[bolt pistol]], as well as frag and krak [[grenades]].{{Fn|1b}} ===Trivia=== {{Trivia}} *The lions of [[wiki:Cithaeron|Kithaeron]] and [[wiki:Nemean Lion|Nemea]] in Greek mythology both had almost impenetrable skin and were both slain by Heracles, who wore the skin of the Lion of Kithaeron as armour ===Sources=== *1: [[The Horus Heresy Book Six - Retribution]]: **{{Endn|1a}}: pgs. 84–91 **{{Endn|1b}}: pgs. 226–227 *{{Endn|2}}: [[The Buried Dagger (Novel)]], Chapters 6–7 *{{Endn|3}}: [[The Horus Heresy: Legions]] [[Category:Characters (Born: Terra)]] [[Category:Characters (Dark Angels)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[fr:Nemean]]

'''Nemeroth''' was a [[Chaos Lord]] and leader of [[The Chosen of Nemeroth]]. Invading the [[Forge World]] of [[Graia]] through a [[Warp]] gate, Nemeroth aspired to ascend to [[Daemonhood]]. Though he would manipulate the [[Ultramarines]] 2nd Company under [[Space Marine Captain]] [[Titus (Ultramarines)|Titus]] into unleashing his horde of [[Chaos Space Marines]], [[Daemons]], and [[The Lost and the Damned|Heretics]] upon [[Graia]], in the end Nemeroth was 'killed' by Captain Titus himself.{{Fn|1}}

It is possible that since Nemeroth was able to partially ascend, and since his voice was heard by Titus moments after he supposedly 'died', Nemeroth may still exist in the [[Warp]] as a Daemon Prince.{{Fn|1}}

==Physical description==
According to his information card from the Anniversary Edition of [[Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine]], Nemeroth stood at 8'8" (2.64cm) tall and weighed 1200lbs (544kg).{{Fn|2}} 

He wore an imposing suit of [[Terminator armor]], which was engraved with many markings and symbols representing his allegiance to [[Chaos Undivided]]. Further strengthening this was the tattoo of the iconic symbol of Chaos, the eight-pointed star, located on his forehead. Nemeroth also boasted dual [[Lightning Claw]]s and appeared to wield powerful psychic abilities.

(Cousin) *[[Lion El'Jonson]]
("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation =[[Chaplain]] of the [[Dark Angels]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Dark Angels]] |Notes = }} '''Nemiel''' was a member of the [[Dark Angels]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{fn|1a}} ===Biography=== Nemiel was formerly a knight of [[the Order]], and later elevated to become a member of the [[Dark Angels]]. Nemiel had a constant rivalry with his cousin [[Zahariel]] lasting from his youth until their separation after the Dark Angels' actions on [[Sarosh]].{{fn|1b}} While occasionally jealous of Zahariel's exploits the two remained very close through all their trials.{{fn|1c}} Only one topic was taboo between Zahariel and Nemiel, and that was Nemiel's participation in the conspiracy to assassinate the [[Emperor]]. Nemiel had led Zahariel to a secret meeting shortly before the Emperor arrived on [[Caliban]]. This meeting was comprised of a few of high ranking members of the recently disbanded knightly orders of Caliban. Some suggested staging an atrocity but it was eventually decided to assassinate the Emperor. Upon hearing this, Zahariel left in disgust and Nemiel quickly followed him. Nemiel promised to dissuade the men of this course of action.{{fn|1d}} Whether Nemiel actually tried is unknown but the attempt on the Emperor was made nonetheless.{{fn|1e}} In the Dark Angel's first deployment with Lion El'Johnson as [[Legion Master]], the 1st Legion fought against the [[Sarosh]] - a bureaucratic people who had been subtly rejecting [[Jaghatai Khan]]'s [[White Scar]]'s in their attempts to bring the world to compliance.{{fn|1f}} After the White Scars departed to continue their campaign, the Sarosh attempted to assassinate Lion El'Johnson and his newly acquired space marines with a nuclear device hidden in the Saroshi diplomat's transport shuttle, thus officially declaring war against the [[Imperium]]. Luther and Zahariel managed to eject the shuttle into space, but in the aftermath Luther confessed to Zahariel that he noticed the bomb beforehand and initially decided to do nothing, admitting that if the Saroshi succeeded in killing the Lion he would get command of the Dark Angels and no longer be forced to live in the Lion's shadow.{{fn|1g}} Sarosh was finally brought to compliance in a decisive battle on one of the planet's orbiting mining stations designated 1Z5 where the Saroshi were attempting to summon a great Chaos [[Daemon]] to slay their enemies. Through the concerted effort of Zahariel and his psyker mentor [[Israfael]], the two were able to conjure a powerful psychic bomb which finally slew the daemon and ended the Sarosh rebellion.{{fn|1h}} Unfortunately this display of psychic energy caused Lion to become wary of the use of Psykers within the Dark Angels. Six hours after the battle on Mining Station 1Z5 Lion El'Johnson, using the excuse of [[Astartes]] recruitment supervision, ordered Luther, Zahariel, their respective commands, and many of the legion's [[Psykers]] to return to Caliban, while Nemiel was selected to stay with the legion during the Great Crusade.{{fn|1i}} Over the five decades that followed, Nemiel was involved in the Legion's deployments on Cyboris and Barrakan, the latter culminating in the [[Siege of Firebase Endriago]] which cemented his status as a model Astartes. He was consequently made a [[Chaplain]], and selected to take part in the Lion's action on [[Diamat]].{{fn|2a}} He was charged with ensuring his brothers were battle-ready, and oversaw logistics and fleet operations as well.{{fn|2b}} Suspecting his Primarch of harboring ulterior motives, he confronted him{{fn|2c}} and was eventually informed of the super-heavy siege vehicles put together by the forge{{fn|2d}}. Nemiel proved instrumental in locating and securing the vehicles{{fn|2e}}, thus unwittingly playing into his Primarch's political maneuvering{{fn|2f}}. Later in the Heresy, as the Dark Angels were battling [[Daemon]]s, the Lion wished to reinstitute [[Librarian]]s to combat them. This was against the edicts of the [[Council of Nikea]], which Nemiel stubbornly reminded his Primarch. In the end, Lion El'Jonson killed Nemiel due to his refusal to back down.{{Fn|3}} ===Sources=== *1: [[Descent of Angels (Novel)]]: **{{endn|1a}}: ''Dramatis Personae'' **{{endn|1b}}: ch. 1 **{{endn|1c}}: ch. 5 **{{endn|1d}}: ch. 16 **{{endn|1e}}: ch. 17 **{{endn|1f}}: ch. 22 **{{endn|1g}}: ch. 23 **{{endn|1h}}: ch. 24 **{{endn|1i}}: ''Epilogue'' *{{Endn|2}}: [[Fallen Angels (Novel)]]: **{{endn|2a}}: ch. 1 **{{endn|2b}}: ch. 3 **{{endn|2c}}: ch. 11 **{{endn|2d}}: ch. 13 **{{endn|2e}}: ch. 17 **{{endn|2f}}: ''Epilogue'' *{{Endn|3}}: [[The Lion (Novella)]], ''IV'' [[Category:Characters (Born: Caliban)]] [[Category:Characters (Dark Angels)]] [[Category:Characters (Deceased)]] [[Category:Characters (Great Crusade)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]]

Nemo.wikitext:
{{NecromundaPortal}}
'''Nemo the Faceless''', named so due to wearing a featureless mask, is the [[House Delaque]] spymaster of [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]]'s [[Hive Primus]] and one of the biggest crime lords on the [[hive world]].{{Fn|1a}}

His vast network of agents gathers information from everywhere within the Hive for him{{Fn|1b}} and Nemo uses this to buy and sell secrets, rumours, half-truths and favours, which he claims are the most valuable commodity of them all.{{Fn|1a}} Not even the private chambers of [[Planetary Governor]] [[Helmawr]] himself are safe{{Fn|1b}} from the rumoured agent of the [[Inquisition]] and anyone who even mentions Nemo's name will be found and marked for death by his agents.{{Fn|1a}}

Nemo has since come into the employ of the [[Inquisitor]] [[Jena Orechiel]], who has ordered him to monitor Kal.{{Fn|2}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was [[Master of the Adeptus Astra Telepathica|Choirmaster]] of the [[Adeptus Astra Telepathica]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].

===Biography===
{{Spoiler|source=The Outcast Dead (Novel)}}
A powerful [[Psyker]], he was romantically involved with [[Aniq Sarashina]], a mistress of the [[Scholastica Psykana]]. He assigned [[Athena Diyos]] to attempt and repair the mind of [[Astropath]] [[Kai Zulane]].{{Fn|1a}} After the [[Drop Site Massacre]], he dispatched the Master of the [[Cryptaesthesian]]s [[Evander Gregoras]] to purge the [[City of Sight]] of [[Astropath]]s afflicted by madness when [[Magnus the Red]] psychically breached the [[Imperial Palace]] to speak to the [[Emperor]].{{Fn|1b}} Later when he discovered that Kai Zulane held information vital to the future of the Heresy, he sent [[Yasu Nagasena]] on a hunt for the Astropath.{{Fn|1c}} After the suicide of Gregoras, Nemo picked up his last journal and began to read what had driven him to it.{{Fn|1d}}

Shortly before the [[Siege of Terra]] Nemo Zhi-Meng reappeared during a meeting of the [[Council of Terra]].{{Fn|2}} He reappeared during another Council meeting during the early stages of the Siege, where he pointed out the Daemonic nature of many of Horus' allies.{{Fn|3}} In the final stages of the Siege, a shuttle carrying Nemo was shot down and recovered by [[Katsuhiro]] and a group of survivors led by [[Euphrati Keeler]] who were being guided by a mysterious light away from the [[Sanctum Imperialis]].{{Fn|4}} 

Alongside [[Sigismund]] and his [[Templar Brethren|Templars]], the group eventually arrived at the [[Hollow Mountain]], where they faced certain death in the face of a massive [[Death Guard]] assault led by [[Typhus]]. During the battle Nemo Zhi-Meng worked closely alongside Dark Angels [[Librarian]]s in reactivating the [[Astronomican]], but not to no avail. However Keeler was able to lead a sacrificial prayer amongst the faithful throngs that caused a psychic backlash which not only threw back the Death Guard but also reactivated the [[Astronomican]]. The prayer caused many of the faithful to disintegrate into dust, Nemo included.{{Fn|5}}
